content.text:
**Finding: Deviation (critical) — § 14.2, ¶ p0054**

Section 14.2 gives Vendor exclusive ownership of every Deliverable created specifically for us, with only a revocable, non-transferable licence for the Order Form term. That fails both the preferred position (Customer ownership with Vendor assignment) and the fallback (perpetual, irrevocable, worldwide, royalty-free, sublicensable licence).

Supporting context:
- § 14.1 and § 14.4 are fine — Customer Data / pre-existing IP ownership is confirmed, and no joint ownership is created.
- §§ 13.2 and 14.3 give a perpetual paid-up licence, but expressly only to *Vendor Technology* embedded in a Deliverable, not the Deliverable itself — so they do not cure 14.2 and sit in tension with it.

Redline validated (ok:true) and submitted: ownership of Deliverables flips to Customer with an express irrevocable assignment, while Vendor's retained Vendor Technology rights under § 14.3 are preserved. The comment offers the licence-back fallback if Vendor insists on retaining title.
